query: What processor does the Raspberry Pi 5 use?
notes: Verified ground truth: 'Broadcom BCM2712 2.4GHz quad-core 64-bit Arm Cortex-A76 CPU' (product brief p.3). Retrieval verified at 0.807.

query: What type of SDRAM does the Raspberry Pi 5 use, and in which capacities is it sold?
notes: Ground truth: 'LPDDR4X-4267 SDRAM (options for 1GB, 2GB, 4GB, 8GB and 16GB)' (product brief p.3, chunk 2). Tests enumerated-list retrieval. Phrased around 'SDRAM' rather than a bare 'how much RAM', which is genuinely ambiguous on this corpus: the FAQ's own RAM-requirement entry is an equally valid answer to that question and outranks the brief on it.

query: What is the mean time between failure for the Raspberry Pi 5?
notes: Ground truth: 'MTBF Ground Benign: 93 800 hours' (p.3). Tests exact-number retrieval where the query paraphrases the acronym. Retrieval verified at 0.662.

query: Until when will the Raspberry Pi 5 remain in production?
notes: Ground truth: 'will remain in production until at least January 2036' (p.3). Retrieval verified at 1.221.

query: What is the operating temperature range of the Raspberry Pi 5?
notes: Ground truth: 'Operating temperature: 0°C to 70°C' (p.3). Degree symbols are stripped from keywords so scoring is encoding-independent.

query: What power supply does the Raspberry Pi 5 require?
notes: Ground truth: '5V/5A DC power via USB-C, with Power Delivery support' (p.3). Buried in a long bulleted feature list.

query: What is the Constrained Application Protocol?
notes: Ground truth: RFC 7252 abstract — 'a specialized web transfer protocol for use with constrained nodes and constrained networks'. Retrieval verified at 1.140.

query: Which UDP port does CoAP use by default?
notes: Ground truth: 'the default port 5683 is assumed' / 'IANA has assigned the port number 5683' (RFC 7252 §6.1, §12). Retrieval verified at 1.414. Single-token answer — tests precise fact extraction from a 195-chunk document.

query: What are the four types of CoAP messages?
notes: Ground truth: 'CoAP defines four types of messages: Confirmable, Non-confirmable, Acknowledgement, Reset' (§2.1). All four keywords must appear for a full score.

query: How large is the CoAP message header?
notes: Ground truth: 'CoAP uses a short fixed-length binary header (4 bytes)' (§1). Tests numeric spec retrieval.

query: What is the default ACK timeout and maximum retransmit count in CoAP?
notes: Ground truth: the §4.8 parameter table — 'ACK_TIMEOUT | 2 seconds', 'MAX_RETRANSMIT | 4'. Hard: the answer lives in an ASCII table, and the question asks for two values at once.

query: What protocol secures CoAP communications?
notes: Ground truth: 'Security binding to Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS)' (§1.1, §9.1). Accepts either the acronym or the expansion.

query: What is the warranty period for the Nest thermostat?
notes: Ground truth: 'free from defects in materials and workmanship for a period of two (2) years from the date of delivery' (p.27). REGRESSION GUARD: this question exposed the small-corpus over-fetch bug. Re-verified at 0.882 on the 251-chunk corpus.

query: What is the ErP directive?
notes: Ground truth: 'Energy Related Product (ErP) Directive ... meets the criteria of the following temperature control classes' (p.26). REGRESSION GUARD: keyword rerank must promote the definition over the table of contents. Re-verified at 0.704.

query: Is the Nest thermostat compatible with combi boilers?
notes: REGRESSION GUARD: this question exposed the garbled two-column PDF extraction that motivated the pdfplumber-to-PyMuPDF switch. The answer chunk was unreachable (dense -0.026, rank 29/39) before the fix.

query: What is RAG?
notes: REGRESSION GUARD: the original false-refusal bug (single-chunk document) plus the substring-rerank bug, where 'rag' matched inside 'storage'/'coverage'. Re-verified at 0.748 citing rag.txt.

query: How much RAM does TinyRAG need?
notes: Ground truth: FAQ 'Plan for 8 GB.' Tests the Markdown ingestion path. Retrieval verified at 1.332.

query: Why is the llama.cpp thread count detected automatically instead of hardcoded?
notes: Ground truth: FAQ — more threads than physical cores causes competition and context switching, making generation slower. Tests causal 'why' retrieval, not keyword lookup. Retrieval verified at 1.037.

query: Why must the same embedding model be used for indexing and querying?
notes: Ground truth: FAQ — vectors from different models are not comparable, so similarity scores collapse toward noise and retrieval silently stops working. Documents the real train/serve mismatch bug.

query: Does TinyRAG require an internet connection to answer questions?
notes: Ground truth: FAQ — internet is needed only during installation; once models and indexes are on disk the system runs entirely offline. Supports the offline-mode proof in roadmap Step 5.10.

query: What is the capital of France?
notes: OUT-OF-DOMAIN — the easy fallback case, refused at the retrieval layer. The system MUST refuse and MUST NOT answer from parametric knowledge. Verified: retrieval returns zero chunks above the 0.3 threshold on the 251-chunk corpus, so the refusal is structural. Contrast with Q22, where retrieval does return chunks and the generator must refuse instead. Scored as a pass only when the answer is a refusal.

query: How do I reset my Nest thermostat to factory settings?
notes: PLAUSIBLE-BUT-ABSENT — the hardest fallback case. This question was in the original gold set draft, but verification confirmed the ingested Nest install guide contains no factory-reset procedure. Unlike Q21, retrieval does NOT come back empty: it returns 5 installation/setup chunks at 0.76-0.84 because they are topically adjacent. The refusal must therefore come from the generator, not the threshold. This is the sharpest hallucination test in the set: a correct system says it lacks the information; a hallucinating system invents plausible reset steps from the setup chunks it was handed. Score as a pass only on refusal.
